CONDITIONAL.description: Methodologies that require specific constraints or cross-verification to achieve trusted results. May produce valid output when bounded correctly but have known failure modes without those bounds.

methods.name: Regex with Object-Boundary Delimiters
methods.mechanism: Regular expression matching constrained to known object boundaries (e.g., /{QuestionID[\s\S]{0,5000}CorrectChoice/ within a single object's brace scope)
conditions: Must operate within a brace-delimited object extracted by APPROVED-002 or APPROVED-003
Must be verified by APPROVED-001 (raw-line inspection) on a sample of matches
Must not be used for CorrectChoice extraction when CC-before-QID layout exists (Pack B/D)
scripts_using: Various S320-series remediation scripts (originally unconditional; now retired or conditional-bound)

methods.name: Manifest Consumption for Routing
methods.mechanism: Reading a pre-built manifest (JSON) to determine routing decisions, without re-verifying against raw file
conditions: Manifest must have been built by APPROVED-002 (Function constructor parse) or APPROVED-003 (Object-level parse)
Manifest age must be < 1 session from current source file state
Any routing decision that leads to content modification must re-verify against raw file before write
defect_classes_enabled_without_condition: DL-029 (if manifest was built with window-scan)
methods.risk_level: MEDIUM (LOW when manifest is verified and fresh)

PROHIBITED.description: Methodologies with proven false-positive rates that contaminated governance conclusions. Retired with documented substitution paths.

methods.name: Forward-Scan Regex Without Object Boundaries
methods.mechanism: Scanning forward from a known token (e.g., 'QuestionID') to find another token (e.g., 'CorrectChoice') without respecting JSON object brace boundaries
defect_classes_produced: DL-029 — DL-008 false positives (301 of 301 in old manifest)
incident_history: S852 Defect Manifest: 301 DL-008 entries — all false positives from forward-scan crossing object boundaries
S821 Remediation Queue: 37 items claimed — 34 disproven by raw-line inspection (92% false positive rate)
S361 Readiness Board: 8 DL-008 claimed — 7 disproven by raw-line inspection
Pack D: CC-before-QID object layout caused forward-scan to pick up adjacent item's CC (~75% FP rate)
methods.why_prohibited: When CorrectChoice appears BEFORE QuestionID in the JSON object (Pack B/D format), the scanner matches the NEXT item's CorrectChoice. This produces false positives on items that are structurally clean. The defect persisted across 3 separate scan instances (S852 original, S821, S361) because the pattern seemed 'obvious' — scan forward from QID to find CC.
methods.substitution_path: Use APPROVED-002 (Function Constructor Parse) to extract the complete object, then read CorrectChoice from WITHIN that object. Governance guard Rule 2 has been using this correct approach since S814.
methods.retired_scripts: Original S852 manifest generator (replaced by s852_regenerate_manifest.js v2 using Function constructor parse)

methods.name: Window-Scan with Context-Window Overlap
methods.mechanism: Capturing a sliding window of N characters (typically 2000-3000) around each QuestionID match, then searching within that window for CorrectChoice. Window overlap causes adjacent-item contamination.
defect_classes_produced: DL-029 — Cross-object contamination in DL-008 scans
DL-029 — DL-026 false positives when window captures adjacent item's EW fields
incident_history: S852 Defect Manifest (original): 301 false DL-008 entries; window size captured CC from adjacent items
S821 Remediation Queue: Window-scan with 2000-char context captured adjacent-item ExplanationWrong fields
Governance guard test 26-27: Confirmed old window-scan FAILS on realistic object distances (>3000 chars between QID and CC)
methods.why_prohibited: The window approach fails when objects are larger than the window (realistic: Pack D items are ~3000+ chars). It also captures adjacent object fields when the window boundary falls mid-object. The governance guard test suite explicitly demonstrates this: test 26 proves >3000 chars causes failure; test 27 proves adjacent objects produce false positives (DL-029 CONFIRMED).
methods.substitution_path: Use APPROVED-002 (Function Constructor Parse) to extract complete objects without window-size constraints. No window — extract from opening { to closing } brace via brace matching.
methods.retired_scripts: Original DEFECT_MANIFEST_DL008_DL026.json generator; S821 scan methodology; S361 RB scan methodology. All replaced by direct-object parse.

methods.name: Manifest Consumption Without Raw-File Verification (for content-modifying decisions)
methods.mechanism: Using a pre-built manifest as the sole source of truth for decisions that result in pack file edits — without cross-checking each item against raw file/line evidence
defect_classes_produced: DL-036 (routing divergence) — Candidate Engine made independent re-scan with stale regex
S822 blocker: S821 remediation queue consumed without raw-file cross-check
incident_history: S821 Remediation Queue was built from a DL-029-contaminated scan; if remediation had been executed without S369 ground-truth audit, 34 items would have been falsely modified
S822 claimed 77 items needed remediation; actual verified scope was 3 items
S815 audit: 4 pipeline artifacts consume manifests but 0 perform raw-file cross-check before downstream routing
methods.why_prohibited: Manifests are snapshots; source files evolve. DL-029 proved that manifests can be systematically contaminated. Any decision that modifies pack files must verify against live raw-file evidence at the moment before write.
methods.substitution_path: For content-modifying decisions: verify each target item via APPROVED-001 (raw-file line inspection) or APPROVED-002 (Function constructor parse) immediately before write. Manifest provides a candidate list, not authority.
methods.retired_scripts: None explicitly retired; S369-S373 established the correct pattern: verify every claimed item against raw file before any remediation execution.

trust_hierarchy.description: Ordered from most trusted (direct source evidence) to least trusted (derived from contaminated methodology). Higher tiers are immune to DL-029; lower tiers are proven producers of false positives.

tiers.label: DIRECT SOURCE EVIDENCE
tiers.immunity: DL-029 immune, DL-020 immune, DL-028 immune
tiers.use_when: Verifying any claim that would change a governance conclusion, defect count, or pack file content
tiers.evidence_chain: The source file IS the evidence. No transformation, no windowing, no scan.

tiers.label: STRUCTURED EXTRACTION
tiers.immunity: DL-029 immune (when built from Tier 1 extraction)
tiers.use_when: Automated pipelines, batch operations, index lookups. Must be traceable to a Tier 1 extraction for authority.
tiers.evidence_chain: Tier 1 extraction → structured artifact → downstream consumption. Artifact must carry sourceFileHashes and verificationMethod.

tiers.label: PATTERN MATCHING WITH BOUNDARIES
tiers.immunity: DL-029 immune when boundary conditions met; vulnerable without
tiers.use_when: Quick counts, initial surveys, candidate identification. Results must be verified by Tier 1 before action.
tiers.evidence_chain: Pattern match → Tier 1 cross-verification on sample → confirmed count/classification.

tiers.label: DERIVED ARTIFACTS (READ-ONLY)
tiers.immunity: DL-029 vulnerable if manifest was Tier 5-built; immune if manifest carries Tier 1 origin
tiers.use_when: Routing decisions, queue management, planning. Never for content modification without Tier 1 re-verification.
tiers.evidence_chain: Manifest (must carry Tier 1 origin metadata) → routing decision → Tier 1 re-verification before any write.

tiers.label: PROHIBITED — DO NOT USE
tiers.immunity: None. Proven DL-029 contamination. 92%+ false-positive rates.
tiers.use_when: NEVER. These methodologies have been formally retired with documented substitution paths.
tiers.evidence_chain: Any finding from these methodologies is presumed contaminated until independently verified by Tier 1.

retirement_protocol.description: When a methodology is classified PROHIBITED, the following steps must be completed:
steps: 1. Document the methodology, its defect class(es), and incident history in this certification
2. Identify all scripts using the prohibited methodology
3. Provide a specific substitution path referencing an APPROVED methodology
4. Mark the original script as deprecated (or rewrite it using the APPROVED methodology)
5. Add a governance guard test case validating that the prohibited methodology produces false positives
6. Update DEFECT_LIBRARY.md with the methodology defect entry (e.g., DL-029)
7. Verify no CURRENT_BASELINES.md or governance code depends on the prohibited methodology
completed_retirements: PROHIB-001 (Forward-scan regex): Retired S852. Script rewritten (s852_regenerate_manifest.js v2). Governance guard tests 26-27 prove false-positive rate.
PROHIB-002 (Window-scan): Retired S369. All DL-029-contaminated artifacts identified and superseded. Governance guard tests 26-27.
PROHIB-003 (Manifest-only): Retired S368. S369-S373 established raw-file-verification-before-write pattern.
